newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL SIGN RIEDLE FROM DORTMUND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL SIGN RIEDLE FROM DORTMUND.

text.p: Liverpool said they had signed Borussia Dortmund's Karl-Heinz Riedle on Wednesday, ending their long search for a striker.

"Roy Evans' summer-long search for a striker has now come to an end, Liverpool have confirmed the signing of Borussia Dortmund striker Karl Heinz Riedle," the premier league club's official telephone information service reported.
It said 31-year-old Riedle, who helped Dortmund win the European Cup by beating Juventus in May, would be paraded at a news conference in Liverpool on Saturday morning.
No figure was given for the signing but media reports put the three-year deal at 1.8 million pounds ($2.9 million).
Dortmund spokesman Josef Schneck said earlier that the clubs had agreed the transfer and Riedle had only to sign.
Liverpool had denied an interest in Riedle earlier this week, despite Dortmund's sports director Ottmar Hitzfeld claiming an approach had been made.
According to German press reports, Riedle -- who scored twice in the Champions' League final -- will be paid an annual salary of 3.7 million marks ($2 million).
He joins former Dortmund team mate Patrik Berger at Liverpool.

Newcastle manager Kenny Dalglish was also believed to have wanted Riedle as a short-term replacement for the injured Alan Shearer while Liverpool manager Evans wanted the German to replace Stan Collymore who has joined Aston Villa.
Dortmund's new coach Nevio Scala backed the move and said his club would now be seeking a new striker.
